headline: Sensex gains 100 points while Nifty trades near 22,700 despite high September foreign outflows and quarterly concerns

marketStatus.message: Market is open for trading today.

why: Foreign outflows from Indian stocks hit a 6-month high in September driven by higher crude oil prices and rising yields.
IT and PSU Bank shares advanced, providing support to the benchmark indices.
Global cues remain mixed, with South Korean stocks erasing gains and Asian markets showing weakness.
Indices face underlying pressure as Sensex and Nifty are on track to record their worst 9-month performance in 15 years.
whatHappening: Sensex gained around 100 points while Nifty moved near the 22,700 mark in morning trade.
Indus Towers signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with Replus Engitech to develop telecom energy storage systems.
Data showed 7 out of 11 recent blockbuster IPOs are currently trading below their respective issue prices.
Vishal Nirmiti IPO opened for subscription today while 5 SME IPOs are scheduled to list on the exchanges.
summary:
Indian benchmark indices opened flat to slightly higher on September 30, with Sensex up 100 points driven by gains in IT and PSU Bank sectors.
However, sentiment remains cautious as foreign outflows hit a six-month high in September due to elevated oil prices and bond yields.
Despite today's modest uptick, Nifty and Sensex are set to post their worst September performance in eight years.
